summary: @or-sdk/payments ships install-time dropper that downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall hook (scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs") runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>, unpacks it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync against a bundled 727KB file math_init.js. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated (string-array-shuffle with rotating array WV8StW, large mixed const array n7gIxM, custom decoder hc1jfK9) and carries a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header confirming it is intended to run under the freshly downloaded Bun binary. Executing an opaque bundled payload via a just-downloaded alternate runtime at npm install time evades Node-based inspection and runs attacker-controlled code with the installer's privileges. The package is published on public npm as @or-sdk/payments, but its CHANGELOG.md references only gitlab.internal.onereach.io — the scope corresponds to an internal-only SDK, consistent with a dependency-confusion lure targeting OneReach.ai developers. A payments SDK has no legitimate reason to download a second language runtime to execute its own obfuscated bundle at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
